paragraphs: An E. coli outbreak linked to frozen blueberries is now over, according to an update from the CDC [1]. The outbreak affected 17 people across two states, with six hospitalizations and no deaths [1].

The FDA issued several Class I recalls this week, the most serious type of recall [2]. Crown Farms Dried Suri Cut, a dried ribbon fish product distributed in Virginia, New York, New Jersey, and Michigan, is being recalled because it was not properly eviscerated before drying [2]. Alfalfa in 50-pound bags from International Sprout Holdings, Inc., sold wholesale across 16 states and territories, is being recalled due to potential E. coli and Salmonella contamination [4]. Momchipz Gluten Free Veggie Chips Broccoli Florets & Cauliflower (3 oz packages, UPC 6 28634 44216 6) sold in the U.S. contain undeclared wheat [3].

Additional recalls include GF Blends Truly AIP All Purpose Flour and Bread Mix and EAT G.A.N.G.S.T.E.R. Flat Bread Pizza Mix due to potential undeclared wheat gluten, which poses a risk to people with celiac disease or severe gluten intolerance [7]. J. HIGGS Loaded Bacon and Cheddar Potato Chips from Saratoga Potato Chips contain undeclared soy [9]. Prolon Everyday Apulian Almond & Cocoa Spread contains undeclared tree nuts including hazelnut, cashew, and pistachio [5], and Fannie May & XO Marshmallow Pixie S'mores Collection contains undeclared milk and pecans [6].
